note: Segment length fractions and densities for the share tests of the volume extractor (volume-extractor brief 4, item 4a). Values are Joe's transcription of the table named below; edition and page are blank until Joe fills them. Nothing here is recalled.
source: Winter, D. A., Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement, Table 4.1 (after Dempster 1955)

uniform_density_basis.source: Dumas et al. 2007, Journal of Biomechanics 40, 543-553 (data/literature/Dumas et al 2007 BSIP Data.pdf)
uniform_density_basis.statement: McConville et al. (1980) and Young et al. (1983) computed the BSIPs assuming a uniform density of 1 g.cm-3; both studies used the same 17 segments, so the sheet's segment masses are volume shares of the reference subjects
uniform_density_basis.consequence: the raw ratio (sheet mass share / sculpt volume share) is the primary test for every segment, shank and foot included; the Dempster-normalised ratio is reported only for the lumped region as a cross-check

dumas2007_table2_source: Dumas et al. 2007, Table 2, female column (Torso = thorax + abdomen)

use.use_note: Winter gives no density for the abdomen or the pelvis alone, only for the two together (1.01); the combined value is applied to each, and the lumped rows use it directly for their abdomen-plus-pelvis part.
